body.statement: Conditional on \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, the interval \(C_\alpha=[\widehat\tau-R_\alpha,\widehat\tau+R_\alpha]\cap[-2B,2B]\) on the regular branch, and \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\) under every declared bad-sample convention, satisfies \[\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\Pr_P\{\tau(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid z_0\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0]\le C R_{\star}^{1/2}.\] The proof must uniformly bound the probability of fewer than two usable blocks, undefined variance denominators, donor-covariance small samples, empty opposite-parity fits, and \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\), and must include the full-range interval's length on those events. Conversely, every interval with the same uniform conditional coverage has worst-case conditional expected length at least \(cR_{\star}^{1/2}\). The \(N^{-\kappa/2}\) expected-length converse, and hence the four-channel length equivalence, uses the maintained direction. The separated calendar-block construction uses actual local-polynomial weights and the full spectrally clipped \(\widehat\Sigma\), and incurs no multiplicative logarithmic phase.
body.justification: Point estimation alone does not resolve whether proxy and spacing bias can be covered honestly without sacrificing a logarithmic factor.
body.gap: Armstrong and Kolesar (2020) calibrate bias-aware intervals after assuming a uniform centered limit, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) handle dependent synthetic-control prediction. Neither derives a phase-uniform shrinking confidence interval for this nonregular causal mean.
body.consumer: The interval gives event-study users conditional coverage and a sample-size diagnostic even when smoothing bias or donor-path uncertainty is first order.
